question.text: The five successive ionization enthalpies of an element are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>800</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2427</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3658</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>35024</mn><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mn>32824</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . The number of valence electrons in the element is:

solution.text: As difference in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>rd</mi></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> ionisation energies is high so atom contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> valence electrons.
